answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers aggregate penalties proportional to k², reflecting pairwise culpability rather than a flat per-node fee. Detection also applies asymmetric depreciation: losses compound across the swarm, creating an exponential multiplier in capital destroyed and making identity-splitting costly. An operator cannot wander through fresh keys to harvest nectar; the attack spiral ends in depleted escrow.
